display.title: The Haggadah Explained in Yiddish, Part 3: The Ten Plagues to Shfoch Chamascha
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children: the Ten Plagues, Dayeinu, Pesach-Matzah-Maror, Hallel, then Motzi Matzah, Korech, the meal, afikoman, bentching and opening the door for Eliyahu.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children, the last of three Haggadah classes begins with spilling wine onto a broken plate at Dam Va'esh and at each of the Ten Plagues, with Rabbi Yehudah's simanim, and the sages' reckoning of fifty, two hundred and two hundred fifty plagues at the sea. The teacher explains the fifteen kindnesses of Dayeinu as a lesson in gratitude, and it is sung. Rabban Gamliel's three things follow: why we eat the Pesach offering, matzah and maror. After B'chol Dor Vador and Lefichach, he explains Hallel, the brachah Asher Ge'alanu and the second cup. The practical part covers Rachtzah, holding all three matzos for HaMotzi, the k'zayis, maror and Hillel's Korech sandwich, the Yom Tov meal beginning with the egg and without roasted meat, eating the afikoman before midnight, pouring Eliyahu's cup, and the Chabad care to keep matzah dry, with a story of the Rebbe Maharash wiping his fork. It ends with bentching, the fourth cup, opening the door for Eliyahu HaNavi and Shfoch Chamascha.
display.lesson: We thank Hashem for every single kindness, and each of us must feel as if he himself left Egypt.

study_text.note: Ten Plagues through Barech and opening the door; Hallel and Nirtzah are not covered.

advisories.note: The Plague of the Firstborn and the Egyptians drowning at the sea, as told in the Haggadah.
